clue.text: Request certain shipboard groups to be heard in floating holiday

parts.note: a request is a plea
certain means sure

indicators.note: the words are to be heard spoken, so the sound of the ship's crews counts rather than their spelling

parts.note: the groups working aboard a ship are its crews

explanation.surface: Someone asks that the ship's crews be audible during a holiday afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be heard' means CREWS is used for its sound only, spelt CRUISE in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure trip on a liner is a holiday spent afloat at sea.

clue.text: Slice of bologna that's needed for biter

indicators.note: a slice is a thin piece cut from the middle of these words, so the letters run across them

explanation.surface: A slice of bologna sausage is all a hungry insect needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slice of' takes the letters from inside 'bologna that's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fly that bites people is a typical biting insect.

clue.text: Decomposition is beginning to spoil lake spit

parts.note: decomposition is rot

indicators.note: the beginning of the word spoil is its opening letter

parts.note: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Rot that starts to spoil a lake sounds like an ecological lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes S from 'spoil'. 'spit' is the roasting skewer, not saliva.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating roasting device is a revolving spit for cooking meat.

clue.text: Church concerned with Birmingham's intellectual centre?

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
RE means about or concerning
Brum is the nickname for the English city of Birmingham

explanation.surface: A church and its role in Birmingham's intellectual life.
explanation.walkthrough: Brum is the informal name for Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest part of the brain handles thought, so it is the seat of the intellect.

clue.text: Part of phone speaker's to hold plug …

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard rather than read, so the word for hold counts by its sound

parts.note: to hold something is to keep it
a plug is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A phone's loudspeaker grips a connector plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' looks like the phone gripping something; it is just KEEP, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttons for dialling numbers form a panel on a telephone.

clue.text: … of which several can be picked up, something like 20

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, so the words count for how they sound

parts.note: several of the previous clue's plugs are ads

explanation.surface: The clue continues the previous one, about several plugs picked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue carries on from 5 Down: 'which' refers to its plug, an advertisement, so several are ADS, heard as ADZE. 20 Across is AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodworking tool with an arched blade is a close cousin of the chopping tool.

clue.text: Work on artist in request to lend animation

indicators.note: the two words before it sit inside the word for request

parts.note: to invite is to request someone's company

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes above it

parts.note: to go is to work, as a machine goes
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist is asked to work on a commission that brings it to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' suggests labour or a creative piece; here it is the verb meaning function, as an engine goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To energize something is to put fresh life and animation into it.

clue.text: Landmark in revolution, having completed year in solitary

indicators.note: the pieces before it go inside the word for solitary

parts.note: solitary means lone
completed means done

explanation.surface: A prisoner marks a full year in solitary confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in solitary' hints at a prisoner's cell, but solitary simply means alone; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant observation wheel on the Thames is a London landmark that slowly turns.

clue.text: Player of M is completely wet, holding back R

indicators.note: holding back the letter means keeping it out of the word

parts.note: to drench is to soak completely

explanation.surface: A soaking actor keeps back the letter R.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding back R' removes R from DRENCH. M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond films.
explanation.definitionFit: Judi Dench played the spy chief M in several James Bond films.

clue.text: Politician coming in has prime minister clutching a tract in the capital

indicators.note: the politician enters the word has

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the prime minister's name grips the letter A inside it

parts.note: Ted Heath was British prime minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A politician arrives while the PM grips a pamphlet in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tract' looks like a pamphlet but is a stretch of land; Ted Heath was Conservative PM in the early 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: The big open heath in north London is a stretch of land within the capital.

clue.text: Having got one's leg over when surge of feeling overcomes resistance

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left

indicators.note: the surge covers and takes in the resistance letter

parts.note: a tide of emotion is a surge of feeling
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A risqué sentence about passion overcoming reluctance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcomes' puts R inside TIDE. The surface reads as sexual innuendo; the definition is simply straddling something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side, as on a horse, means one leg has been swung across.

clue.text: Retiring actor who doesn't speak with BBC accent receives plummy bonus

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole run is read in reverse
the silent actor takes the plummy letter inside

parts.note: a mime is an actor performing without words
U means upper-class, as a plummy voice is
RP, Received Pronunciation, was the traditional BBC accent

explanation.surface: A shy silent actor with a posh accent gets a fruity bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reverses the whole run, giving MUIMERP read backwards; RP, Received Pronunciation, was the old BBC standard.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra sum paid on top of the normal price or wage is a bonus.

clue.text: University that is excluded from regular feature on Telly Addicts?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is is shut out of the regular feature

parts.note: a series is a regular programme on television
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A university is barred from appearing on a TV quiz about television fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' removes IE from SERIES. Telly Addicts was a BBC TV quiz show; here 'Addicts' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug addicts are often called habitual takers, a sense of the word for consumers.

clue.text: Take care from Stelios budget deer-minding service?

parts.note: Stelios Haji-Ioannou founded the budget easyJet brand
a doe is a female deer
to sit is to mind, as in babysit

explanation.surface: A budget-brand tycoon launches a service that looks after deer.
explanation.walkthrough: Stelios's easyJet empire names its budget services 'easy...'; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a gentle instruction to go slowly and carefully.

clue.text: They're foremost in displays, among tail-trailing lines?

definitions.text: They're foremost in displays, among tail-trailing lines?

indicators.note: the lines trail behind, coming after the tail
the picked letter goes among the other letters

parts.note: the rear is the tail end

indicators.note: the foremost letter of the word displays

parts.note: rows are lines

explanation.surface: Aircraft lead air displays with coloured trails streaming behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foremost in' picks D, placed 'among' REAR followed by ('trailing') ROWS. The whole clue also describes the RAF aerobatic team and their smoke trails.
explanation.definitionFit: The RAF's aerobatic team are the leading air-display act, trailing coloured smoke.

clue.text: Routine character played by Routledge with son in old vehicle?

indicators.note: the son letter goes inside the word for routine

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine
Patricia Routledge played Hyacinth Bucket in the sitcom Keeping Up Appearances

explanation.surface: A sitcom actor's routine character and her son appear in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyacinth Bucket was the snobbish heroine of the BBC sitcom Keeping Up Appearances. 'in' puts S inside RUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrepit, corroded car is slang for an old banger of a vehicle.

clue.text: Back away from other clubber, perhaps

indicators.note: the back of the word, its final letter, goes away

parts.note: else means other, as in someone else

explanation.surface: Advice to step back from another nightclub-goer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Els is a South African golfer, so a 'clubber' who swings clubs, not a nightclubber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Els, the golfer, wields golf clubs for a living.

clue.text: Kirk's helmsman again docked over home planet of Star Trek race

definitions.text: home planet of Star Trek race

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the run reads backwards

parts.note: Sulu was helmsman under Captain Kirk on the Enterprise

indicators.note: docked means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: more means again, as in once more

explanation.surface: Captain Kirk's helmsman docks again on an alien world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' trims MORE to MOR; SULU MOR is then reversed by 'over'. Romulans are a Star Trek race.
explanation.definitionFit: In Star Trek, the Romulans come from the planet named after Rome's founder.

clue.text: Something wished on lucky actor or spinner

definitions.meaning: actors are told to break a leg as a good-luck wish
in cricket a ... is a ball spun from the leg side, and its bowler

explanation.definitionFit: Theatre folk wish each other luck by saying break a leg; in cricket the term is a slow bowler's spinning delivery.

clue.text: Weapon that would be carried by Xena repeatedly

indicators.note: the weapon is carried inside the doubled name, so only the letters across the join are kept
the warrior princess's name is written out twice in a row

parts.note: Xena is the warrior princess of the TV series, taken as her name's letters

explanation.surface: Xena the warrior princess keeps carrying her weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Write XENA twice, XENAXENA; the weapon sits across the join, once the outer XEN and NA are dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A chopping tool with a blade on a handle can serve as a battle weapon.

clue.text: End regime in corrupt state, providing compensation

indicators.note: corrupt here means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to topple a corrupt regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in corrupt state' rearranges END REGIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A redeeming feature makes up for faults, offering compensation.

clue.text: Will leaves most ready to scoff

indicators.note: the word Will goes away from the longer word

parts.note: most willing means readiest

explanation.surface: A man named Will walks out on someone eager to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will leaves' removes WILL from WILLINGEST; 'to' is a link. 'Will' looks like a name or a testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it greedily, taking it into the body.

clue.text: Sort of weak, unreliable person abandoning five characters after the start

indicators.text: abandoning five characters after the start
indicators.note: the five letters straight after the first are dropped

parts.note: a broken reed is someone who cannot be relied on

explanation.surface: A feeble person loses five characters early in a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning five characters after the start' drops ROKEN from BROKEN REED.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed is a kind or type, as in a rare breed.

clue.text: In charge of work unit about to endure shipping hazard?

indicators.note: the work unit goes about the word for endure

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics
to be is to exist or endure

explanation.surface: A supervisor at a work unit is set to endure a danger to shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shipping hazard?' carries a question mark because the definition is by example; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating masses of ice threaten ships, as the Titanic found.

clue.text: We're thrown in jug

indicators.note: thrown means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We find ourselves thrown into a jug, or jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' rearranges WERE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A large wide-mouthed pitcher is a kind of jug.

clue.text: Violence finally enters sports ground I have to fence

indicators.note: the final letter goes into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: rec is short for recreation ground
I've is I have contracted

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of violence

explanation.surface: Violence breaks out at a sports ground that I must enclose with fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E, which 'enters' REC plus IVE. 'fence' is a dealer in stolen goods, not a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a criminal who takes in stolen goods.

clue.text: Minimal statement in the red, streamlined music gadget?

OD is short for overdrawn

explanation.surface: A bank statement shows a tiny overdraft, alongside a sleek music player.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'statement' is a bank one: overdrawn by just 1p, 1p O/D. 'statement' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's slim portable music player is a pocket gadget.

clue.text: Banish half of team, keeping the same number

only the first half of the number word is used

parts.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives ELE, the first half of the team word ELEVEN; 'the same number' is eleven again, in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to send someone into forced absence from their country.

clue.text: Sons limit subject to whipping boy

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

the ego is the self, the thinking subject
at can stand for to, as in at home

explanation.walkthrough: A whipping boy was once punished for a prince's misdeeds.
